validated_results.title: Cancer incidence in Mormons and non-Mormons in Utah, 1966-1970.
validated_results.journal: The New England journal of medicine
validated_results.reason: The comparison is by religious affiliation (Mormon vs non-Mormon) rather than measured alcohol intake, so alcohol is only an incidental proscription with no alcohol-specific prostate cancer estimate.

validated_results.title: Effect of a vegetarian diet and dexamethasone on plasma prolactin, testosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone in men and women.
validated_results.reason: The study reports only hormone changes (prolactin, testosterone, DHEA) in healthy volunteers on a vegetarian diet, with no prostate cancer incidence outcome.

validated_results.title: Mechanism of action of diet as a carcinogen.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of concepts and mechanisms of diet as a carcinogen rather than an original human study with prostate cancer incidence data.

validated_results.title: Diet and urinary steroids in black and white North American men and black South African men.
validated_results.reason: The study measures urinary steroid hormone excretion under vegetarian and Western diets and explicitly leaves the relationship to prostate cancer development unclarified, providing no incidence results.

validated_results.title: Diet and urinary steroids in black and white North American men and black South African men.
validated_results.reason: Only urinary androgen and estrogen levels are reported for men fed a Western diet, with no prostate cancer incidence outcome measured.

validated_results.title: Epidemiology of prostate cancer with special reference to the role of diet.
validated_results.reason: The measured exposure was daily intake of green and yellow vegetables with vitamin A only mentioned speculatively as a possible explanatory factor, and the reported endpoint was the age-standardized prostate cancer death rate rather than a vitamin A-specific incidence estimate.

validated_results.title: Liver cirrhosis, tobacco, alcohol, and cancer among blacks.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
validated_results.reason: The analysis compares relative frequencies of cancer sites among cancer patients with and without cirrhosis, which is a prevalence-type distribution rather than prostate cancer incidence in relation to alcohol.

validated_results.title: Cancer of the prostate: early diagnosis by zinc and hormone analysis?
validated_results.reason: Zinc and androgens were measured in prostatic tissue specimens for discriminating benign hyperplasia from carcinoma, offering diagnostic rather than incidence evidence.

validated_results.title: Cancer of the prostate in blacks.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
validated_results.reason: The publication presents two non-comparative case reports with a literature review and only a general recommendation about zinc supplements, with no original incidence analysis.

validated_results.title: Cancer of the prostate in blacks.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
validated_results.reason: The article is a two-case report with narrative literature review lacking any comparative zinc exposure estimate for prostate cancer incidence.
